problems.locator: PDF p. 17, Section 3.2, high-quality human perspective-taking rate; definition on PDF p. 12, Section 2.4
problems.quote: group-AI condition (M = 0.17, SD = 0.38) and the human-only group condition (M = 0.24, SD = 0.38), F(1, 47) = 0.91, p = 0.345.
problems.note: This contrast is incorrectly omitted in not_extracted as a process measure. Section 2.4 defines the rate by originality and usefulness scores on ideas participants adopted into their task output, with both scores required to be at least three. Thus it is an output-quality outcome answering with_ai. Section 3.2 reports the condition comparison separately from the mediation analyses, with no participant subgroup or mediator-adjusted effect specified. Restricting the outcome to peer-derived ideas does not make the comparison a participant-subgroup analysis. Rule 4 requires this contrast; Rule 5 does not exclude an otherwise eligible output-quality comparison merely because the paper calls the measure perspective taking. Preserve uncertainty about the analysis unit and do not derive people counts from the ANOVA degrees of freedom.

problems.locator: PDF p. 18, Section 3.2, high-quality AI perspective-taking rate; definition on PDF p. 12, Section 2.4
problems.quote: group-AI condition (M = 0.82, SD = 0.29) significantly outperformed those in the individual-AI condition (M = 0.33, SD = 0.26), t(142) = -10.23, p < 0.001, d = 1.78
problems.note: This contrast is incorrectly omitted in not_extracted as a process measure/mediator. It measures the share of AI-derived ideas adopted into participants’ output that meet the originality and usefulness thresholds, so it is an output-quality outcome answering with_ai, with comparison_type ai_design. The independent-samples comparison printed in Section 3.2 is separate from the mediation effects in Section 3.4. Subsequent use as a mediator does not exclude this standalone comparison under Rule 5; Rule 4 requires it. Retain the negative t statistic exactly as printed and note its sign differs from the treatment-minus-control ordering of the means. The paper uses an independent-samples test despite its repeated-condition design, and does not establish this test’s independent analysis units; se_basis should be unclear. Do not infer people counts from df = 142 or silently treat this test as paired.

summary: Checked all 12 estimates after reading the complete 374-line markdown conversion, including the references; the saved 31-page paper has no appended appendix. Opened all cited estimate-source pages (7, 8, 10, 15 and 16) with pymupdf and checked the surrounding methods and results. All recorded numerical statistics match the PDF and the named arms. The 96-person final sample and completion of all three conditions support the repeated-condition people counts, without establishing independent outcome-row counts or SD levels. Found five problems: high-quality idea fluency is miscoded as construct other in three contrasts, and two eligible contrasts on the quality rates of adopted ideas are omitted. Ordinary fluency is reported only verbally, so its null effect statistics are appropriate.
